items.stem: A finance team wants to compare the cost of leasing versus buying a machine over five years. Which technique is most appropriate?

options.text: Net present value of the cash flows under each option
options.rationale: Correct: discounting the cash flows of each option to present value allows a like-for-like comparison.

options.text: Comparing only the first-year cash outflow
options.rationale: A single year ignores the multi-year cash flows and the time value of money.

options.text: Choosing whichever has the lower sticker price
options.rationale: Sticker price ignores financing, maintenance and timing of cash flows.

options.text: Picking the option with the higher accounting depreciation
options.rationale: Depreciation is a non-cash allocation and is not the deciding cash-flow criterion.

items.explanation: Correct: discounting the cash flows of each option to present value allows a like-for-like comparison.

items.stem: In a rolling forecast, how often is the forecast horizon typically updated?

options.text: Once at the start of the fiscal year only
options.rationale: That describes a static annual budget, not a rolling forecast.

options.text: Continuously, adding a new period as each one closes
options.rationale: Correct: a rolling forecast always extends the horizon as each period completes.

options.text: Only when actuals differ from budget by more than 20%
options.rationale: Rolling forecasts update on a regular cadence, not only on large variances.

options.text: Never; forecasts are fixed once approved
options.rationale: Fixed forecasts are the opposite of the rolling approach.

items.explanation: Correct: a rolling forecast always extends the horizon as each period completes.
